This is a capital cost percentage based on historical data for similar operations. • Administrative and support labor – Covers the cost of overhead for marketing, administration, and office support. • Property tax and insurance – They include the cost of insurance and tax for the assets. This is typically a percentage of capital cost. • Consumables – Consumable costs include all non-fuel costs like utility consumption, catalysts, solvent consumption, and processing. The initial fill of the catalyst and solvent is considered under capital cost. However, any make-up or replacement over the life cycle is covered under consumables cost. • Fuel includes the cost of natural gas or any other fuel used in the system. • Co-product or by-product credit – Revenue from Co-products is credited to arrive at the effective cost of production of the primary products. The rest are variable costs. 9.2 Assumptions The key considerations for capital cost estimate are as follows: • Bare Erected Cost (BEC) estimate for the entire project is developed using vendor data, in-house databases, and commercial software packages. While this cost estimate represents the best possible estimate considering the current level of detailing, the actual cost may vary depending on site-specific factors, implementation considerations, and design changes. • Direct Labor costs for equipment installation and construction costs for foundations and buildings are based on the ‘parametric estimate method’ using the in-house database for similar installations. • The estimated cost is 2022 US$ basis • Engineering, Procurement, and Construction Management Fees have been considered at 15% based on the experience of the Recipient in designing, engineering, and building similar projects. • Since carbon capture technology has not been commercialized yet, a ten (10) % process contingency has been considered for the carbon capture unit. However, other components of the projects, like the gas turbine, steam boilers, compressors, water gas shift reactors, etc., have been commercialized and running at multiple places for decades and more. Accordingly, process contingency for those units has been considered at ‘Zero.’ And project contingency is calculated considering 10% of EPC cost plus process contingency. • For the Owner’s cost estimate, detailed guidelines and assumptions are given in the QGESS document. All the assumptions are consistent with the guideline. However, royalties for equipment are included in equipment cost; no provision has been made for the same.
